items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: Of course after World War II then there was this big building boom, and so this fella Doelger, he built — he developed the Sunset and also the area where San Francisco State is, Stonestown, Daly City.

ctx.x: Well yes. I’m a native born San Franciscan, I was born in 1920, January the 29th, and there have been many, many, many changes. Everything. Our skyline has changed, it’s been Manhattanized, our transportation system, which used to be the best in the country, we’re having problems with it. We went from all electric streetcars and cable cars and we went to buses and we do have light rail now but it’s in trouble, our municipal railway. We have an underground, which we never had before, then we have of course the…

grew up — and you’ve got the Richmond District, that’s going out to the beach say from Presidio Avenue west and that’s on the north side of Geary Blvd. Then you have the Sunset District. Now the Sunset District would be beyond our deYoung museum in the past, that would be going west, and on the opposite side of the park, the south side of the park, all of that area. Now that area, when I was growing up, was sand dunes. They had sand dunes. You had streets but you had sand dunes. And when you’d take people out, if…
Right. You can only go so far.
